key_insight: An adaptive strong-form phase-field solver localizes fine resolution to a narrow moving interface using gradient smoothing and layered mesh refinement, cutting cost while preserving accuracy.
engineering_relevance: This enables scalable simulation of interface-dominated mechanics and materials problems where uniform fine meshes would be prohibitively expensive.
method: Couple Gradient Smoothing Method (GSM) with a hierarchical adaptive and moving structured mesh.
Use layered refinement to keep locally uniform spacing across the diffuse interface.
Maintain coarse resolution in bulk regions to reduce degrees of freedom and improve scaling.
evidence_signal: Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard tests show the adaptive GSM solver retains desired interface-evolution accuracy while achieving near-linear O(N) computational complexity.
watch_item: GSM has a higher cost per degree of freedom than standard finite-difference methods, so performance depends on effective mesh adaptation and interface localization.
paper_title: An adaptive phase field framework for large-scale interface evolution problems using a strong-form gradient smoothing approach
